Exceptions & Signature carve-outs

Author WAF exceptions and signature customisations as desired state bound to Server Policies, then push them to the FortiWeb, place them on other FortiWebs, version, roll back and safely delete them.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsprotection.view protection.edit protection.apply advisor.use operations.template_approve
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → Operations → WAF → Exceptions & Signature (URL /exceptions/<id>)

What is it?#

A Web Protection Profile is usually shared by several Server Policies, and FortiWeb keeps no record of which policy an exception was written for. The Exceptions & Signature page records that intent in SATOM: each carve-out (a WAF exception or a signature customisation) is stored as desired state, bound to one or more Server Policies, and pushed to the appliance only when you explicitly ask.

What does it do?#

  • Authoring — a typed form for ten WAF exception types and eight signature types, bound to a Web Protection Profile and to Server Policies, with a reason.
  • Team rules enforced by SATOM 1. Templates stay clean — a carve-out cannot target a profile governed by an approved template; the save is refused and a guided clone is offered. 2. Lifecycle — re-binding a Server Policy to another profile in SATOM marks its carve-outs STALE (never deletes them); purging a policy previews what is deleted and what is only unbound. A change made on the device itself, outside SATOM, is flagged DRIFT (see Carve-outs that no longer match the device). 3. Capacity — a signature set takes at most 128 exception entries; the push refuses beyond that, and the guided clone checks profile capacity.
  • Push — Inject writes one carve-out onto the device after a dry-run preview.
  • Detect — reads per-signature exceptions already on the device and imports the ones you pick.
  • Deploy — places a carve-out on other FortiWeb scopes as desired state.
  • History — every change is versioned; roll back to an earlier version or restore a deleted carve-out.
  • Safe delete — an impact report before every delete.
  • Analyse before implementing — an advisory that explains how wide the carve-out reaches, optionally with an AI opinion.
Category Types
exception HTTP Protocol Constraints · Allow Method · Geo IP Block List · Syntax-Based Detection · Bot Mitigation · HTTP Header Security · Cookie Security · URL Encryption · Link Cloaking · File Security
signature Signature Exception (per-id) · Disabled Signature · Alert-Only Signature · Disabled Sub-Class · Custom Signature · Custom Signature Condition · Custom Signature Group · Class Action Override

Requirements#

  • A selected FortiWeb. Without one, the page redirects to the Service Diagram to pick a device.
  • For the profile and policy pickers, Inject, Detect and the impact report: the device must be reachable. The page still opens when it is not; the pickers are then empty.

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open the page, filters, version history, diff, impact report, deploy destinations, inject targets, Analyse before implementing (SATOM's own analysis) protection.view
The Assistant (AI) opinion in Analyse before implementing advisor.use
Save carve-out, Delete, Clone one per policy, Purge, Preview the clone / apply, Inject (dry-run and push), Deploy (preview and place), Roll back, Restore, Run detect, Import selected config_write

config_write comes from protection.edit or protection.apply — or from any other *.edit / *.apply key, such as network.edit. The page does not distinguish authoring from pushing: either key unlocks both.

Without config_write the page is read-only: Edit, Inject, Deploy and Delete are hidden on the rows, and Save carve-out and Detect on device are greyed out with the tooltip Needs the config_write permission. Purge, Roll back and Restore stay visible; the server refuses them with 403 Forbidden.

Analyse before implementing sends the draft to the configured AI provider only for users with advisor.use. Everyone else, and every user when no provider is configured or enabled, gets SATOM's own analysis only.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the AI opinion in Analyse before implementing now requires advisor.use, and users without config_write no longer see the write buttons that would only fail.

How to use#

Author a carve-out#

  1. Open Operations → WAF → Exceptions & Signature.
  2. In New carve-out, choose the Type. The form loads the fields that type needs; fields that take a regular expression have a .* button that opens the Regex Lab.
  3. Choose the Web Protection Profile. A profile marked 🔒 template is template-managed; see the guided clone below.
  4. Optionally enter Name (optional) and describe What problem is this meant to solve?.
  5. Select the Server Policies under Bind to Server Policies (Ctrl/Cmd for several) and enter a Reason.
  6. Optionally click Analyse before implementing (see below).
  7. Click Save carve-out. The carve-out appears under Authored carve-outs.

To change one, click Edit on its row. The type cannot be changed.

Analyse before implementing#

The advisory returns SATOM's own analysis — the breadth of the carve-out, what it Stops and what it Keeps, structural concerns, and other exception types whose description matches your problem. When an AI provider is available and you hold advisor.use, an Assistant opinion follows. It never blocks a save: This is advisory. Nothing has been saved or pushed.

Template-managed profile — guided clone#

  1. Save a carve-out against a template-managed profile. SATOM refuses it and opens 🔒 Template-managed profile — guided clone.
  2. Check the Clone name (pattern from Naming → Exception WPP, default wpp-<policy>). A Server Policy must be selected first — the clone is named after it.
  3. Click Preview the clone. SATOM reads the appliance and lists the sub-objects it will copy under the policy's own names and those it cannot copy (they stay shared), each with a reason. Tick any overridable ones you want copied anyway.
  4. Click Apply — copy N object(s), re-bind & save. SATOM clones the profile on the device, re-binds the Server Policy to the clone, and re-submits your carve-out against it.

The button is disabled when the device's profile capacity is reached: WPP capacity limit reached — free capacity first (see /capacity). See Capacity and Policy cloning.

Push a carve-out to the device (Inject)#

  1. Click Inject on the row.
  2. In ⬆ Inject to device choose the Target object on device. For signature exceptions each set shows its usage, for example (120/128 exceptions); full sets are disabled and marked FULL.
  3. For container types tick Create the target object if it doesn't exist if needed.
  4. Click Dry-run preview to see the plan, then Push to device and confirm Push this carve-out onto the device?.

Import what is already on the device (Detect)#

  1. Click Detect on device, then Run detect. SATOM walks server policy → profile → signature set → filter list.
  2. Tick the rows to keep and click Import selected. Entries already recorded for the same profile, signature and policy are skipped.

Place a carve-out on other FortiWebs (Deploy)#

  1. Click Deploy on the row. Every visible FortiWeb scope is listed with a verdict: Ready to place, Already has this carve-out, Profile is template-managed, Profile not recorded on this scope or Source scope.
  2. Select destinations, click Preview, then Place on selected scopes.

Placing is not pushing. Each placement is recorded as desired state on its scope and must be injected from that scope.

Delete safely#

  1. Click Delete. The panel What deleting this would take away shows a verdict: - Safe to delete — offers Delete; - Needs review before deleting — offers I have read the above — delete anyway; - Cannot delete — clone per policy first — offers Clone one per policy (N), which splits the carve-out into one copy per Server Policy.
  2. Confirm Delete this carve-out?.

If the carve-out predates version history the panel warns that deleting it cannot be undone.

Carve-outs that no longer match the device#

When the page opens, SATOM reads the device's Server Policies and the Web Protection Profile each one uses, and compares them with the carve-outs. A carve-out is flagged DRIFT when none of the Server Policies it names still binds its profile on the device: the policy is gone, or now uses another profile. That change was made on the device itself, outside SATOM, where the STALE hook never ran.

  • A banner says <n> carve-out(s) no longer match the device — a Server Policy they name is gone or now uses another Web Protection Profile. It changed on the device, outside SATOM. Re-point each one at the policy's current profile, or delete it. Show them filters the list to those carve-outs.
  • Each one carries a DRIFT badge next to its category.
  • Any state → not on the device applies the same filter.
  1. Click Show them (or choose not on the device and Filter).
  2. Edit each carve-out and point it at the profile its Server Policy uses now, or delete it.

Nothing is flagged when the device's policy list could not be read (the device does not answer), for a carve-out already flagged STALE, and for a carve-out bound to no Server Policy. Nothing is changed on the device or in SATOM: the flag is computed each time the page opens.

History, rollback and restore#

  • The clock button opens Version history. Diff vs current compares a version with the carve-out as it is now; Roll back appends a new version with the earlier body — nothing is deleted.
  • Deleted carve-outs that can still be brought back → Show them → Restore re-creates a deleted carve-out with the bindings it had.

The firmware build a carve-out was written for#

A FortiWeb answers a write carrying a field its build does not know with 200 and discards the field, so a carve-out written on one build and pushed to another could land without the field that made it a carve-out. Every carve-out (and its fleet library item) therefore records the firmware build and REST API version of the appliance it was authored on:

  • a copy placed on other FortiWebs keeps the source build;
  • editing the payload restamps it; rollback and restore bring back the build of the old payload (the stamp is versioned, but kept out of the content hash);
  • Inject and the Attack ID insert check the payload against the target's running build: a field the build discarded, renamed or does not serve blocks the push. A user with operations.template_approve can override with a reason, audited as exception.compat.override.

The API sweep does not measure the carve-out sub-tables yet, so most pushes show no evidence — a warning, never a pass.

Purge a Server Policy#

  1. Under Purge (clean migration) choose the Server Policy and click Purge.
  2. SATOM shows which carve-outs would be DELETED (nothing else binds them) and which UNBOUND (they still serve another policy). Confirm to apply.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Type The carve-out type (fixed once saved) Yes Signature Exception (per-id)
Web Protection Profile The profile the carve-out lives on No (empty is allowed) wpp-shop
Name (optional) Display name No checkout-sqli-fp
What problem is this meant to solve? Free text used only by the analysis No checkout POST trips a signature
Bind to Server Policies One or more policies No (shown as unbound) shop-www
Reason Why the carve-out exists No Confirmed false positive, ticket 1234
Type fields The FortiWeb fields of the type; validated on save Per type signature_id

Example#

🧪Example — Per-policy signature exception on a shared profile

wpp-shop on fweb-01 is bound by shop-www and shop-api. An operator authors a Signature Exception (per-id) for signature 010000001, bound to shop-www only, and saves it. Inject → target the signature set → Dry-run preview shows the POST; Push to device writes it. Later, re-binding shop-www to another profile in SATOM flags the carve-out STALE; the operator edits it to point at the new profile, which clears the flag.

Result#

  • Saves, edits, deletes, splits, deploys, rollbacks and restores change SATOM's database only; creating, updating and deleting a carve-out each record a version.
  • Inject and the guided clone write to the appliance.
  • Audit entries include wpp_exception.delete, wpp_exception.purge, wpp_exception.deploy, wpp_exception.rollback and wpp_exception.restore.

Troubleshooting#

""" is a template-managed Web Protection Profile — templates stay clean (no exceptions)…"#

Possible causes — the chosen profile is governed by an approved template.

Solution — use the guided clone, or choose a non-template profile. If the message ends with Select the Server Policy first — the clone is named after it., bind a policy and save again.

Verification — the carve-out saves against the cloned profile.

"Signature set "" already holds 128/128 exception entries — FortiWeb rejects more. Remove an entry first."#

Possible causes — the target signature set is full.

Solution — remove an unused exception entry from the set, or choose another set.

"no server policies / device unreachable"#

Possible causes — Run detect could not read any policy binding.

Solution — check the device is reachable and has server policies, then run detect again.

"This delete needs an explicit acknowledgement."#

Possible causes — the impact verdict is Needs review before deleting (the profile is shared, or the device could not be read).

Solution — read the reasons and use I have read the above — delete anyway.

"nothing to split — this carve-out is bound to fewer than two policies"#

Solution — the split is only for carve-outs bound to several policies; delete or edit it instead.

"choose at least one destination"#

Solution — tick at least one scope in the Deploy panel.

"type cannot be injected"#

Possible causes — SATOM has no device mapping for this carve-out type.

Solution — create it in the FortiWeb GUI or in the Web Protection editor.

A carve-out shows STALE#

Possible causes — its Server Policy was re-bound to another profile after it was authored.

Solution — Edit it and choose the new profile (saving clears the flag), or delete it.

"<n> carve-out(s) no longer match the device"#

Possible causes — a Server Policy the carve-out names was deleted on the device, or re-bound there to another Web Protection Profile, outside SATOM.

Solution — click Show them, then Edit each carve-out to use the policy's current profile, or delete it.

Verification — after a reload the banner and the DRIFT badge are gone.

Advanced Internals
  • Carve-outs live in SATOM's database (wpp_exceptions plus a policy junction table). There is no record of whether one was pushed.
  • Every delete goes through the impact check (guarded-delete) and writes an audit entry; the former unchecked POST /exceptions/<id>/delete was removed in 2.11.0. Delete and save by id refuse a carve-out that belongs to another device than the one in the URL.
  • The device target of an Inject is chosen at push time and never stored.
  • The impact report reads live policy bindings; when the device cannot be read, sharing is treated as unknown, never as "not shared".
  • Deploy uses the stored configuration snapshots to tell whether the profile exists on a destination; a destination with no snapshot is let through as unknown.
  • POST /exceptions/<id>/clone-exception (a private copy for one Server Policy) exists as an API call; the page itself uses the split.
